def: Blockbuster’s name for a late fee: a charge when a rental was kept past its due date.
A one-time payment to shareholders, made outside the regular dividend.
A way for a parent company to give up a subsidiary by letting its shareholders swap parent shares for subsidiary shares.
A deal in which a rental chain pays a studio a smaller price up front and shares the rental income afterward.
Bonds that are repaid after secured and senior debt if the borrower cannot pay everyone.
A write-down of an asset’s recorded value when the company judges it to be worth less than that.
A liquid that carries a weak, invisible gel structure. It pours like a liquid but stops suspended particles from sinking.
A gel-forming hydrocolloid that the Associated Press named as the material of the Orbitz spheres.
The smallest force a gel-like liquid needs before it starts to flow. Below it, particles held in the liquid stay where they are.
The study of how materials flow and deform.
Pieces of solid matter, such as fruit bits or gel spheres, suspended in a drink.
The industry label for premium non-cola drinks such as flavored sparkling water, iced tea and functional drinks.
The annual report that a company based outside the United States files with the SEC when its shares trade in the US.
A report in which such a company furnishes news, such as press releases, to the SEC.
An electronic quotation service for shares that are not listed on a major exchange.
The filing that proves a trademark is in commercial use. An applicant who filed before using the mark must send it after the notice of allowance or the application is abandoned.
Sales minus the cost of goods sold, usually shown as a share of sales. What counts as a cost of goods sold varies by company.
The costs a company books directly against the products it sells. Whether shipping, warehouse labor and delivery belong here is a choice each company makes and discloses.
Storing, picking, packing and shipping orders. For an online retailer it is either its own cost line or part of another one.
Statements prepared for a company that is winding down. Assets are shown at what they are expected to fetch, and there is no profit and loss, only changes in net assets.
What is expected to be left for owners after the estate sells assets and pays its debts.
The filing that legally ends a Delaware corporation, which can then only wind up its affairs.
A short SEC filing in which a large shareholder reports how much of a company it owns.
The registration statement a company files with the SEC before selling shares to the public.
The filing that ends a company's duty to file periodic reports with the SEC.
Financial statements shown as if a deal had already happened, with adjustments to make two companies' books comparable.
Chewy's name for scheduled repeat deliveries. Pets.com, PetSmart.com and Petopia each described a similar program in their filings.
